sources.entry: Pixtamer - Batch convert, compress, resize and rename images into web-ready JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF, with responsive widths and presets.

summary.one_liner: Pixtamer is a free, open-source native macOS app that batch converts, compresses, resizes and renames images into web-ready JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF files, entirely on the local Mac.
summary.what_it_does: Pixtamer takes batches of images and converts them to JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF, with options to compress, resize and rename outputs. It can generate responsive width variants and save reusable presets. Exports include real before and after sizes, and the README describes safe exports with collision policies that protect source files. Processing runs locally with no account, no upload and no network access. The processing logic lives in a separate PixtamerKit Swift package that is tested without the UI, with 97 tests reported in the README. Diagnostics can be copied from the Help menu for bug reports and contain no images or full file paths.
use_cases: batch convert photos to webp or avif for a website
compress and resize a folder of images
generate responsive image widths for web pages
rename image files in bulk with consistent naming
convert HEIC photos to JPEG on a Mac
prepare offline images without uploading them
how_to_run: Download the latest Pixtamer-.dmg from Releases, open it and drag Pixtamer to Applications.
open Pixtamer.xcodeproj # then Run the "Pixtamer" scheme
notable: Runs fully on-device with no account, upload or network access
WebP encoding via bundled, unmodified libwebp 1.6.0
AVIF option appears only if the Mac's encoder passes a launch-time test
Reusable presets and responsive width variants
Processing logic is separated into a UI-independent Swift package with 97 tests
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later; AVIF availability depends on macOS version and was verified only on macOS 27
WebP output has no metadata or colour profile; 16-bit/HDR sources export as 8-bit and animated GIFs export only the first frame; RAW and PSD are not accepted
PNG output is lossless only, so photos saved as PNG are often larger; not yet verified on macOS 14/15, with VoiceOver, or with very large batches
